value.text:
The user wants me to act as Evidence Critic and check each claim against the cited evidence. I need to flag only factual problems: overstatements, wrong numbers/dates/suppliers, causes not stated, products/NDCs not in evidence. Reasonable conclusions from cited facts are supported.

Let me examine each claim:

Claim 1: investigator: "Our package NDC 44567-510-01 is not on the FDA shortage list." Cited: [search-shortage-4]

Evidence says: "Searched this run's FDA shortage list snapshot for our package NDC 44567-510-01 and product 44567-510: not on the list."

Matches exactly. Supported.

Claim 2: investigator: "Current stock of 8 units provides 8.3 days of cover at 1 unit per day." Cited: [stock-4]

Evidence says: "cisplatin CISPLATIN 1 mg/mL (WG Critical Care, LLC, NDC 44567-510-01, NDA018057): 8 units on hand, 1/day over 30 days, 8.3 days of cover; open orders: PO-SAMPLE-004 backordered 11 units from McKesson, expected 2026-10-20"

Matches exactly. Supported.

Claim 3: investigator: "No ongoing recall for this NDC." Cited: [search-recall-4]

Evidence says: "Searched this run's FDA ongoing-recall snapshot for our package NDC 44567-510-01 and product 44567-510: no ongoing recall."

Matches. Supported.

All claims appear supported. No factual problems. So unsupported list empty.

I must reply with JSON: {"unsupported":[]}.</think>{"unsupported":[]}
